title: Perfect tenses: negatives, questions and little words
intro: Read this before the questions on the present perfect and the present perfect continuous.

blocks.title: present perfect
items: **Negative:** subject + **have / has** + not + past participle: She **hasn't seen** it.
**Question:** **Have / Has** + subject + past participle: **Has** she **seen** it?
**Continuous negative:** have / has + not + **been** + verb-ing: I **haven't been sleeping**.
**Continuous question:** **Have / Has** + subject + **been** + verb-ing: **Have** you **been waiting**?

blocks.title: where the little words go
items: **never, just, already, always:** between the helper and the participle: I have **never** seen it. She has **already** left.
**ever:** in questions, after the subject: Have you **ever** been to Rome?
**yet:** at the END, in questions and negatives: He hasn't called **yet**. Has he called **yet**?
**How long** + have / has + subject + participle: **How long have** you **lived** here?

blocks.title: the slips
items: **One negative per clause:** I **have never** seen it, or I **haven't ever** seen it. Not *I haven't never seen it*.
**yet** goes with questions and negatives; **already** goes with positive sentences.
A finished time (yesterday, last year, two days ago) needs the past simple: **Did** you see it yesterday? Not *Have you seen it yesterday?*
For a situation that continues, ask with the perfect: **How long have you lived** here? Not *How long do you live here?*
